title: Falling OATs And A Divided France
text:
Falling OATs And A Divided France

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 25 Aug 2026

About 20 kilograms ago, I served in the Mountain Infantry Division of the French army, at a time when the French military was professionalizing. As a young second lieutenant, I was lucky enough to have at my side a terrific sergeant-major. He was straight out of central casting: handlebar mustaches, chipped front tooth, spiders tattooed on his knuckles, proudly anti-English, and the deepest voice I had ever heard, resonant enough to leave the barrack walls shaking. He had started off in the Foreign Legion, and had served in Gulf War I, then in Africa, in Yugoslavia, in Guyane...At the time, I was a big supporter of the army’s professionalization. As I saw it, asking guys who did not want to be there to put on a uniform for a year made no sense, especially in an age of increasingly high-tech warfare. In my view, if France was to have the best army she could have, then that army needed to be run by professional soldiers. The end of conscription was clearly a good thing.
